claims.text: Real-time in situ ML-controlled electrochemical synthesis can direct the formation of noble-metal high-entropy-alloy three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Dynamic adjustment of synthesis parameters improves atomic precision in NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
Dynamic adjustment of synthesis parameters produces more uniform porous architectures.
Improved atomic precision and uniform porous architecture enhance catalytic activity.
The starting material is a homogeneous noble-metal precursor alloy solution or deposit containing the constituents required for an NM-HEA.
The electrochemical synthesis uses cyclic voltammetry with a sweep rate of approximately 0.1 V/s.
Controlled current densities are used during synthesis.
Real-time ML feedback continuously adjusts potential limits and other reaction parameters.
In situ electrochemical signals can provide suitable real-time input to an ML control algorithm.
The three-dimensional nanoframework forms through selective dealloying and structural reorganization.
Dynamic electrochemical control promotes selective dealloying and structural reorganization.
An ML model can identify electrochemical signals indicative of selective elemental removal.
An ML model can identify electrochemical signals indicative of structural reorganization.
ML-directed adjustment of potential and current density promotes formation of a porous, well-organized three-dimensional nanostructure.
A porous, well-organized three-dimensional nanostructure provides enhanced atomic-level control.
ML-controlled synthesis will yield more uniform and atomically precise NM-HEA nanoframeworks than conventional open-loop synthesis.
ML-controlled NM-HEA nanoframeworks will exhibit greater catalytic activity than frameworks made by open-loop methods.
The effectiveness of the method depends on obtaining high-quality real-time in situ characterization data.
The effectiveness of the method depends on the ML model correctly interpreting and responding to synthesis signals.
